lesson.summary: Secure workloads by layering controls: segment networks with subnets, security groups, and network ACLs; keep traffic private with NAT and VPC endpoints; filter web traffic with AWS WAF and Shield; detect threats with GuardDuty and Inspector; and manage credentials with Secrets Manager and IAM roles.
keyPoints: Security groups are stateful and allow rules only; network ACLs are stateless with allow and deny rules
Reference security groups as sources to restrict tiers
NAT gateway gives private subnets outbound-only internet access
Gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB are free and keep traffic private
WAF filters layer 7 requests; Shield protects against DDoS
Secrets Manager rotates database credentials automatically
GuardDuty detects threats, Inspector finds vulnerabilities, Firewall Manager applies policies centrally

scenarios.text: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets behind an Application Load Balancer. The application connects to an Amazon RDS database using a password that is hardcoded in the code. Compliance now requires the password to rotate every 30 days, and no long-lived AWS access keys may be stored on the instances.

questions.prompt: A three-tier application has public web servers, private application servers, and a private database. The database must accept connections only from the application servers, even if their IP addresses change. What is the best way to configure this?

options.text: Allow the application subnet CIDR range in the database network ACL only
Allow 0.0.0.0/0 on the database port and rely on the database password
Reference the application tier security group as the source in the database security group inbound rule
Place the database in the public subnet with an elastic IP address

questions.explanation: Security groups can use another security group as a source, so only members of the application tier can connect regardless of their IPs. A subnet-wide network ACL rule is broader and stateless. Opening to the internet relies on only one control. A public subnet with an elastic IP exposes the database unnecessarily.

questions.prompt: EC2 instances in a private subnet must download operating system patches from the internet, and the internet must not be able to initiate connections to them. Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Attach an internet gateway and give each instance a public IP address
Create a VPC peering connection to the default VPC
Add a Site-to-Site VPN connection
Deploy a NAT gateway in a public subnet and route the private subnet's default route to it

questions.explanation: A NAT gateway allows outbound internet access from private instances while blocking unsolicited inbound connections. Public IPs on instances make them reachable from the internet. Peering and VPN do not provide internet egress for patches.

questions.prompt: A public web application behind an Application Load Balancer is being probed with SQL injection and cross-site scripting requests. Which service blocks these requests with the least operational effort?

options.text: AWS WAF with managed rule groups associated to the ALB
AWS Shield Standard
Amazon GuardDuty
A network ACL that denies the attacker IP addresses

questions.explanation: AWS WAF inspects HTTP requests at layer 7 and managed rule groups cover common injection and XSS patterns. Shield Standard protects against network and transport layer DDoS, not application payloads. GuardDuty detects threats but does not block requests. Network ACLs cannot inspect request content and attacker IPs change.

questions.prompt: A Lambda function runs in private subnets with no internet route and must write to Amazon S3. The company wants the lowest cost and traffic that stays on the AWS network. What should the architect add?

options.text: A NAT gateway in each Availability Zone
An S3 interface endpoint with a per-hour charge
A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 and a route table entry for it
An internet gateway with a public IP on the function

questions.explanation: A gateway endpoint for S3 adds a route to the private subnets, keeps traffic on the AWS network, and has no additional charge. A NAT gateway adds hourly and per-GB charges. An interface endpoint works but adds hourly cost. Lambda functions in a VPC do not get public IPs, and an internet gateway would not fix that.

questions.prompt: Which TWO actions help protect an internet-facing web application from DDoS attacks? (Choose two.)

options.text: Place CloudFront in front of the application and enable AWS Shield Advanced on it
Add an AWS WAF rate-based rule to limit requests per IP address
Open all ports in the security group so legitimate traffic is not blocked
Disable logging to reduce load
Move the application to a single larger instance

questions.explanation: CloudFront absorbs traffic at edge locations and Shield Advanced adds enhanced DDoS protection and response support, while a WAF rate-based rule throttles abusive sources. Opening all ports increases exposure. Disabling logging removes visibility. One larger instance remains a single point that can be overwhelmed.

questions.statement: Security groups are stateful, so return traffic for an allowed inbound request is automatically allowed, whereas network ACLs are stateless.
questions.explanation: True. Security groups track connections, while network ACLs evaluate inbound and outbound rules separately and need both directions allowed.

questions.prompt: Match each AWS security service to what it does.

pairs.right: Detects threats by analyzing CloudTrail, VPC flow, and DNS logs
Scans EC2, ECR images, and Lambda for software vulnerabilities
Managed stateful and stateless traffic filtering for a VPC
Centrally applies WAF and security group policies across accounts

questions.explanation: Each pairing matches the service description in the AWS documentation.

questions.prompt: Where should the application store the database credentials to meet the 30-day rotation requirement with the least operational overhead?

options.text: In an encrypted file in the application's S3 bucket
In the EC2 user data script
In environment variables baked into the AMI
In AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation enabled

questions.explanation: Secrets Manager stores credentials and can rotate supported database secrets on a schedule using managed Lambda functions. Files in S3, user data, and AMI variables all require custom rotation and spread plaintext copies.

questions.prompt: How should the EC2 instances be authorized to retrieve the secret without storing any access keys?

options.text: Attach an instance profile role that allows secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on that secret only
Create an IAM user and store its keys in the Auto Scaling launch template
Make the secret readable by everyone through a resource policy
Copy the secret value into each instance at launch by hand

questions.explanation: An instance profile role supplies temporary credentials and can be scoped to one secret for least privilege. IAM user keys in the template are long-lived credentials. A public resource policy exposes the secret. Manual copying is error prone and defeats rotation.

questions.prompt: A company wants to inspect all outbound traffic from many VPCs and allow only specific domain names, with intrusion prevention rules and centrally managed policy. Which service fits best?

options.text: Security groups on every instance
AWS Network Firewall
Amazon Inspector
Network ACLs with allow rules for each IP

questions.explanation: AWS Network Firewall provides stateful inspection with domain-list filtering and intrusion prevention, and it can be managed centrally. Security groups cannot filter by domain name. Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, not traffic. Network ACLs match IPs and ports only and cannot follow changing domain IPs.
